slides.title: LF AI & Data Foundation Welcomes AIRSEAI to Unite Open Source Embodied AI Ecosystem
slides.highlight: The addition of AIRSEAI to the LF AI & Data Foundation supports the development of an open source embodied AI ecosystem, which is relevant to RwB's focus on embodied social robots.

slides.title: RoboColiseum Launches Standardized Simulation Platform for Embodied AI Evaluation
slides.highlight: RoboColiseum has launched a standardized simulation platform for evaluating embodied AI, providing a framework relevant to the embodied social robots and interaction goals of RwB.

slides.title: Predicting Turn-Taking Outcomes in Multi-Party Conversation: Interpretable Modelling of Speech and Gaze Dynamics with Interpersonal Closeness
slides.tldr: PREDICTING MULTI-PARTY TURN-TAKING VIA GAZE AND SPEECH
slides.highlight: This research models how gaze, speech loudness, and interpersonal closeness signal floor changes in multi-party dialogue, contributing to HyECHO's focus on multimodal social perception and addressee modeling.

card.one_liner: Multimodal modeling of gaze and speech intensity predicts whether multi-party conversation transitions result in gaps or overlaps.
card.key_idea: Regularized logistic regression using gaze entropy, NMF/PCA-reduced gaze bigrams, speaker loudness (Phon), and perceived interpersonal closeness (IOS) to classify floor-transfer outcomes.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on the GaMMA corpus using LOGO/LOCO cross-validation. Multimodal model achieved ROC AUC 0.76 ± 0.04, significantly outperforming the gaze-only baseline (0.58 ± 0.05).

slides.title: Synthetic Linguistic Agency: How an Embodied Mortal Agent Learns Linguistic Affordances through Consequential Social Experience
slides.tldr: EMBODIED MORTAL AGENT LEARNS SOCIAL LINGUISTIC AFFORDANCES
slides.highlight: This research introduces an Embodied Mortal Agent (EMA) that learns to adapt its speech based on bodily consequences and social history, providing insights into embodied social robots and human-robot interaction for RwB.

card.one_liner: Introduces Synthetic Linguistic Agency (SLA) and an Embodied Mortal Agent (EMA) that learns language through survival.
card.key_idea: MGL-RL couples a mortal body with a Bayesian controller, where linguistic choices are valued by their predicted effect on the agent's remaining useful life (Reference-RUL).
card.evaluation: Controlled experiments using a cohort of EMAs, involving interventions on body state and biography to trace causal contributions of embodiment, participation, and precariousness.
card.limitation: The study uses a controlled simulation with scripted partner policies and a limited action repertoire rather than open-ended human interaction.

slides.title: TurnBench: A Multi-Domain Benchmark for Turn-Taking Dynamics in Spoken Dialogue
slides.highlight: TurnBench provides a hand-labeled corpus and evaluation protocol for end-of-turn and interruption detection, supporting HyECHO's focus on listener modeling and engagement in hybrid human-AI teams.

card.one_liner: TurnBench is a multi-domain benchmark for evaluating end-of-turn and interruption detection in spoken dialogue.
card.key_idea: A 30-hour triple-annotated corpus across six interaction styles with a unified evaluation protocol to benchmark heterogeneous turn-taking systems against linguistically grounded labels.
card.evaluation: 14 systems were evaluated on a speaker-disjoint test set using recall, false positive rate, and latency; VAP performed best.
card.limitation: Data is limited to English, dyadic, studio-recorded conversations and lacks a methodology for evaluating interruptions in full-duplex models.

slides.title: Pose-Anchored Optical Flow for Low-Latency Human Action Anticipation in Human-Robot Teaming
slides.highlight: PoseOFF uses pose-anchored optical flow to capture local motion around joints, enabling earlier human intent understanding for more responsive human-robot interaction. This is relevant to RwB's focus on embodied social robots and human-robot interaction.

card.one_liner: PoseOFF improves early human action anticipation by anchoring local optical flow features to skeletal joints.
card.key_idea: It samples small optical flow windows around human keypoints, creating a compact, body-aligned motion representation integrated into skeleton-based models via a lightweight CNN embedding layer.
card.evaluation: Tested on NTU RGB+D 60/120 and UCF101 using InfoGCN++, MS-G3D, and ST-GCN++. Results show improved accuracy at early observation ratios and higher AUC.
card.limitation: Less effective under severe occlusion or for actions dominated by large-scale global motion patterns.

slides.authors: Lewis de Zoete Grundy et al.

slides.title: AffectSim: A Controllable Interactive 3D Simulation Benchmark for Embodied Affective Perception
slides.tldr: CONTROLLABLE 3D BENCHMARK FOR EMBODIED AFFECTIVE PERCEPTION
slides.highlight: AffectSim provides a 3D simulation environment to study how agent viewpoint and sensing influence emotion perception, supporting the RwB goal of improving human-robot interaction.

card.one_liner: AffectSim is a 3D simulation benchmark for studying how embodied agent movement improves affective perception.
card.key_idea: It decouples affective human motions from 3D scene observations, allowing the same emotion-labeled behavior to be re-observed under varied distances, orientations, and occlusions.
card.evaluation: Evaluated 24 frozen perception models on 27,647 episodes. Results show active observation improves Macro-F1 for 21/24 configurations, recovering part of the observation-quality gap.
card.limitation: Currently focuses on the perceptual layer with prescribed affective behaviors; non-repeating or temporally evolving behaviors are not yet included.

slides.title: How Much Can AI Understand? Toward AI-Assisted Sensemaking of Collaborative Discussion in Groups with Shared History
slides.highlight: This work proposes a model for AI-assisted sensemaking that captures group norms, participants, and social context, aligning with HyECHO's focus on group norms and social perception.

card.one_liner: Proposes an AI sensemaking model that incorporates social context and shared group history into collaborative discussions.
card.key_idea: An AI-assisted model supporting early sensemaking stages (extraction, prioritization, connecting, presentation) by integrating arguments with community norms, participant context, and domain-level discussion topics.
card.evaluation: Based on two studies of experienced Wikipedia editors' cognitive processes and a web-based LLM-assisted prototype; results are not quantitatively detailed.
card.limitation: High system interpretive work risks dehumanizing participants, creating false consensus, and biasing results toward contributions most legible to the AI.

slides.title: The Shape of Power: A Multilingual Framework for Social Power Reasoning in Dialogues
slides.highlight: This work introduces a framework for analyzing social power and power asymmetry in multilingual dialogues, contributing to HyECHO's goals of understanding group norms and social perception.

card.one_liner: A multilingual framework and dataset for reasoning about social power dynamics in movie dialogue.
card.key_idea: Combines a social-science grounded schema (demographics, power types, speaker dynamics) with a native-speaker annotation pipeline and custom interface for cross-cultural analysis.
card.evaluation: Evaluated 6 LLMs/MLLMs against human annotations on French and Egyptian Arabic datasets using Gwet’s AC2 and Jaccard similarity; models struggled with implicit power.
card.limitation: Limited to two languages and two annotators per scene, potentially restricting generalizability and the range of interpretive perspectives.

slides.title: Generative Action-Chunk Sampling for Adaptive Stiffness Control in Physical Human-Robot Collaboration
slides.tldr: ADAPTIVE STIFFNESS CONTROL VIA GENERATIVE SAMPLING
slides.highlight: This research introduces a framework that uses variation in sampled action chunks to adapt robot stiffness, enhancing compliance during physical human-robot interaction. This is relevant to RwB's focus on embodied social robots and human-robot interaction.

card.one_liner: Adaptive robot stiffness control using variation among sampled action chunks to balance assistance and compliance in pHRI.
card.key_idea: A CVAE-based policy samples multiple action chunks from an observation-conditioned prior; high sample variance triggers lower stiffness for human guidance, while low variance increases assistance.
card.evaluation: Real-world collaborative transport task (4 directions); proposed method achieved 0.95 success rate vs. 0.83 (fixed-stiffness ablation) and 0.69 (deterministic FACTR).
card.limitation: The action-deviation signal is a proxy for behavioral alternatives, not a calibrated probability of intention or epistemic uncertainty.

slides.title: Counterfactual Bias Testing for Application Tracking System
slides.tldr: LLM-AGENT BASED BIAS AUDITING FOR CANDIDATE-JOB MATCHING
slides.highlight: This work introduces a methodology using LLM agents to synthesize resumes for counterfactual bias testing in job-matching systems, supporting MIMIC's focus on societal-scale impact analysis of AI agents.

card.one_liner: A framework for auditing AI hiring systems using LLM-generated synthetic resumes to detect demographic bias.
card.key_idea: A two-phase LLM agent pipeline synthesizes identity-neutral base resumes and injects demographic variants, evaluating them via a nine-metric fairness suite and semantic ranking.
card.evaluation: Tested on 5 job orders, 100 base candidates, and 10 bias treatments; used bootstrap confidence intervals and significance tests (e.g., Wilcoxon, McNemar).
card.limitation: The qualification-preservation check is currently lightweight and lacks rigorous quantitative validation against a large, human-curated real-resume benchmark.

slides.title: A Shaky Voice Is Not Always a Dodge: Benchmarking Textual and Vocal Evasion Detection in Earnings Calls
slides.highlight: This work introduces DualEvasion, a benchmark for detecting evasion using both text and vocal confidence, contributing to HyECHO's focus on multimodal social perception and engagement.

card.one_liner: DualEvasion benchmarks textual and vocal evasion in earnings calls, revealing a significant gap in audio-based confidence detection.
card.key_idea: A dual-label dataset (textual evasion and vocal confidence) used to test if multimodal models can detect speaker-relative prosodic cues versus absolute acoustic values.
card.evaluation: Zero-shot testing of LLMs and audio models on 505 Q&A pairs; textual evasion showed high F1 (up to 87.4), but vocal confidence lagged (max 58.5).
card.limitation: Small sample size (60 calls) and time-intensive annotation process limit scalability and the statistical power of market relevance analysis.

slides.title: When Robots Mishear Us: Mapping the Safety Risks of Voice-Controlled Embodied AI
slides.tldr: ASR ERRORS INCREASE EMBODIED AI SAFETY RISKS
slides.highlight: This research demonstrates how automatic speech recognition errors can cause embodied AI to execute harmful instructions or bypass safety refusals, which is critical for the development of safe social robots in RwB.

card.one_liner: ASR errors in voice-controlled embodied AI can bypass safety filters and trigger harmful physical actions.
card.key_idea: Simulated ASR errors (acoustic substitutions, noise, etc.) were injected into safety benchmarks to test if corrupted text weakens model refusal and planning robustness.
card.evaluation: Evaluated using POEX and SafeAgentBench with Qwen2.5-7B and GPT-4 variants. Metrics included Acceptance Rate, Executable Success Rate, and planning success rates.
card.limitation: Automatic ASR correction is not always effective, particularly when input semantics are heavily damaged by high-strength noise.

slides.title: Counterfactual Explanations and the Scope of Contestability
slides.tldr: ENHANCING ALGORITHMIC CONTESTABILITY VIA COUNTERFACTUAL EXPLANATIONS
slides.highlight: This research explores how counterfactual explanations can reinstate human agency by enabling the contestability of algorithmic decisions. It is relevant to MIMIC's focus on the impact analysis of hybrid human-AI societies.

card.one_liner: Analyzes whether counterfactual explanations effectively enable users to contest automated algorithmic decisions.
card.key_idea: Defines contestability as providing sufficient information to revoke decisions and proposes a multi-shot querying approach to improve counterfactuals' ability to detect algorithmic errors.

slides.authors: Alice C. W. Huang et al.
